item.text: {"schema":"voice-draft-source/3","kind":"draft","ledger":[{"id":"c1","basis":"request-supported","claim":"Owning a device should include control over whether its maker can disable features after sale.","request_basis":"arguing that owning a device should include control over whether its maker can disable features after sale"}],"paragraphs":[{"sentences":[{"text":"Here’s the puzzle: when you buy a device, what exactly have you bought?","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c1"]},{"text":"You’ve paid for the object in your hands, but the argument here is that ownership should include control over whether its maker can disable features after sale.","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c1"]},{"text":"That sounds obvious until you notice the little trapdoor beneath the word “own.”","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]}]},{"sentences":[{"text":"If a maker can reach into a device after the sale and switch off something you bought, then your ownership is conditional (and the condition is controlled by someone else).","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"You can hold the device, carry it around, customize it, and depend on it, while the maker retains a remote hand on the controls.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"That’s less like owning a tool than renting a room whose landlord can rearrange the furniture whenever it suits them.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]}]},{"sentences":[{"text":"Of course, makers need room to fix defects, address security problems, and change services that genuinely can’t remain frozen forever.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"I’m not arguing that every feature must last unchanged for eternity.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"I’m arguing for a boundary: fixing a problem is different from withdrawing a capability, and maintaining a device is different from quietly reducing what it can do.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"Those distinctions matter because the buyer has already made the central bargain.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]}]},{"sentences":[{"text":"What happens when the feature you rely on becomes a permission the maker can revoke?","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"You’re left with the physical shell of your purchase and a software-shaped “maybe” hovering over it.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"The device still looks like yours, but its useful boundaries have been redrawn somewhere you can’t see.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"That’s the bullshit at the center of control without ownership.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]}]},{"sentences":[{"text":"We should be especially suspicious of the phrase “after sale.”","basis":"normative","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"The sale is the moment when money, expectation, and responsibility are supposed to line up.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"You pay, the maker provides the thing, and we understand what each side is allowed to do next.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"If the maker can later disable a feature, then the transaction hasn’t ended in the ordinary sense; it has become an ongoing negotiation in which you’ve already paid and the other side still holds the veto.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]}]},{"sentences":[{"text":"I think the technical question is simpler than the industry-shaped fog around it.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"Can the device continue doing the thing you bought it to do without asking permission from its maker?","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"If the answer depends on a remote decision, an account status, or a change you can’t inspect, then the problem isn’t merely inconvenience.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"It’s that the device’s behavior has been separated from your control.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]}]},{"sentences":[{"text":"You might say that the maker created the feature, so the maker should be free to remove it.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"That confuses authorship with authority.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"A maker can design a capability, document it, and support it, while the buyer still receives a reasonable claim to keep using it (subject to clear, narrow limits).","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"We don’t treat every purchased object as a temporary invitation to the seller’s future preferences.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"A maker’s continuing involvement can be valuable, but it shouldn’t turn the buyer into a guest in their own device.","basis":"normative","claim_ids":[]}]},{"sentences":[{"text":"I want to stress the practical consequence for you.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"When you choose a device, you’re also choosing a relationship with the maker’s decisions.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"That relationship should include updates and repairs, but it shouldn’t include an invisible button marked “make this purchase smaller.”","basis":"normative","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"Our devices shouldn’t become evidence lockers for promises that can vanish later.","basis":"normative","claim_ids":[]}]},{"sentences":[{"text":"The rule we need is modest: owning a device should include control over whether its maker can disable features after sale.","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c1"]},{"text":"That rule leaves room for safety fixes, honest end-of-support policies, and features that were plainly temporary from the start.","basis":"normative","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"It simply says that a sale should transfer meaningful control, not just possession.","basis":"normative","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"You shouldn’t have to keep proving that you own the thing you already bought.","basis":"normative","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"If ownership can be switched off, it was never ownership in the first place.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]}]}],"omitted":[],"refused":""}
